title: shadow-oncall-handoff-and-game-day-scorer
author: Elena García
body:
Overview

This playbook captures a reproducible, low-friction process for shadow-oncall handoffs, bridge startup, and structured game-day scoring. It is intended for SREs, first responders, and service owners who participate in rotational oncall (primary/secondary/observer). The document bundles: a pre-bridge checklist, rapid-triage commands and runbook invocation guidance, a game-day scorer to evaluate readiness, a compact postmortem template, and canned status page & customer comms language.

Scope
- Applies to all Redwood Inference production-facing services (hosted API, dedicated pools, private control plane).
- Focuses on incidents impacting SLOs, throughput, or customer-affecting errors (tier 1–2).
- Not intended for developer-local failures or CI-only incidents.

Service SLOs & Pager Triggers (examples)
- Availability SLO: 99.95% monthly per-region. Pager if availability drops below 99.8% for 15 minutes.
- Latency SLO: p95 < 300ms, p99 < 900ms. Pager if p95 increases > 2x baseline for 10 minutes.
- Error SLO: client error rate (4xx) < 0.5% and server error rate (5xx) < 0.05%. Pager if 5xx > 0.5% for 5 minutes.

Roles & Responsibilities
- Primary responder (oncall): owns triage, runbook execution, and initial comms.
- Secondary (escalation): provides deep-dive support and coordinates fixes.
- Bridge operator (bridge lead): runs conference bridge, status page updates, and stakeholder notifications.
- Observer / shadow: absorbs context, executes checklist items delegated by primary, and fills game-day scorecard.
- Service owner: accountable for post-incident actions and runbook updates.

Prerequisites (for the shadow)
- Ensure you are a member of the service Slack channel and have bridge access (Zoom/Google Meet + bridge template).
- Have access to runbook links, Grafana dashboards, SLO dashboards, and incident ticketing (Jira).
- Confirm MFA, VPN/VPC access, and kube/gcloud/aws creds are valid.

Shadow Handoff Checklist (pre-bridge)
1) Pre-Bridge sync (5 minutes)
   - Confirm current alert: name, severity, time triggered.
   - Retrieve primary summary: what’s known / impact matrix (tenants, regions).
   - Validate metrics: check p95/p99, error spikes, CPU/GPU throttles.
2) Environment sanity (3 minutes)
   - Run quick health checks (commands below).
   - Confirm no planned maintenance windows overlapping (PagerDuty schedule & infra calendar).
3) Communication plan (2 minutes)
   - Confirm bridge link, set Slack channel to private incident thread, and prepare initial status page template.
4) Delegation agreement (1 minute)
   - Agree which runbook tasks the shadow will own (e.g., logs collection, tenant impact table).

Quick Triage Commands & Shortcuts
- Fetch recent 5xx count (example):
  curl -s 'https://metrics.redwood.internal/api/query?query=service:requests:5xx:sum&range=10m' | jq
- Retrieve last 2m of bridge logs for request-id X:
  rg \"request_id=REQUEST_ID\" /var/log/bridge/*.log | tail -n 200
- Check KV cache eviction rate (if applicable):
  promql: sum(rate(kv_cache_evictions_total[5m])) by (instance)
- Restart inference worker (use with caution; consult runbook):
  rwnctl -s <service> restart-worker --worker-id $ID --grace 30

Runbook Invocation & Verification
- Always record: time invoked, actor, runbook link, and any deviations.
- Invocation steps:
  1. Confirm pre-conditions listed in runbook (e.g., sufficient tokens in queue, DB replica status).
  2. Execute the first non-destructive verification action and capture output as artifact (logs, screenshots, grafana snapshots).
  3. If verification fails, escalate to secondary and avoid blind changes.

Artifact collection checklist (shadow tasks)
- Tenant impact table: tenant name, region, endpoints affected, estimated % of traffic impacted.
- Grafana snapshots: p95/p99 charts, request rate, error rate, host CPU/GPU utilization.
- Logs: selected spans containing error signatures and correlation IDs.

Bridge Startup Script (template)
1. Create incident ticket (Jira) with summary: [INCIDENT] <service> — <short impact>
2. Start bridge using incident bridge template and paste:
   - Incident ID, ticket link, primary, secondary, bridge link
3. Post initial status (internal Slack): short impact + mitigation in progress + expected update cadence.
4. For external customer-visible incidents, prepare a status page stub and legal/compliance notification (if regulated tenant involved).

Game-Day Scoring Rubric (1–5, documented by shadow)
Purpose: objective evaluation of readiness during drills and real incidents. Use the rubric to inform retro and training priorities.
- Time-to-acknowledge (Target: <= 2m)
  5 = acknowledged in < 30s, 4 = < 1m, 3 = < 2m, 2 = < 5m, 1 = > 5m
- Initial diagnosis quality (Target: concise RCA hypothesis + data)
  5 = precise hypothesis + supporting metrics/logs, 3 = plausible but missing artifacts, 1 = no hypothesis
- Runbook fidelity (Target: invoke correct runbook and follow it)
  5 = invoked and logged deviations, 3 = partially followed, 1 = ad hoc changes without logging
- Communication cadence (Target: updates every 15m at minimum)
  5 = updates on cadence + customer-facing draft, 3 = intermittent, 1 = silence > 30m
- Artifact completeness (Target: tenant table + grafana + logs)
  5 = all artifacts collected, 3 = some artifacts, 1 = none

Scoring example (fill in immediately post-incident):
- Time-to-acknowledge: 4
- Initial diagnosis quality: 3
- Runbook fidelity: 5
- Communication cadence: 4
- Artifact completeness: 5
- Total: 21/25 — training focus: diagnosis tools and alert signal tuning.

Compact Postmortem Template (use as Jira/Confluence page skeleton)
- Title: Postmortem — <service> — <short impact>
- Severity: P1/P2
- Incident window: <start> — <end> (UTC)
- Impact summary: short bullet list (tenants, requests impacted, user-visible effects)
- Timeline (minute-granular): numbered entries with actor and artifact links
- Root cause hypothesis: concise statement
- Contributing factors: 3–6 bullets (monitoring blindspots, coupling, capacity decisions)
- Immediate mitigations during incident: bullets and timestamps
- Long-term actions (owner, due date, verification criteria): table-like formatted list
- Game-day scorecard: paste the filled rubric and commentary
- Customer communications: paste the exact status page & email sent
- Evidence: links to grafana snapshots, logs, and runbook invocations

Action tracker format (copy into Jira/Confluence table)
- Action: short description | Owner: name | Due: YYYY-MM-DD | Verification: how we will validate | Status: todo/in_progress/done

Status Page & Customer Communication Templates
- Status page short form (initial):
  Summary: We are investigating elevated error rates for the Redwood API in US-west-2.
  Impact: Some requests may result in 5xx errors or slower responses.
  Next Update: in 15 minutes.
  Components affected: Hosted API — inference-service-us-west-2
- Status page visible update (after mitigation):
  Summary: Reduced error rates after a targeted rollout pause; recovery in progress.
  Impact: Partial — customers on dedicated capacity may have experienced failed requests between 11:02–11:24 UTC.
  Mitigation: We paused the 2.1.3 worker rollout and reverted to 2.1.2.
  Next Steps: Monitoring for stability; full postmortem to follow.
- Customer email (template for customers with SLA concerns):
  Subject: Incident update: Redwood API — partial errors in US-west-2 — {Short ID}
  Body: Hello {CustomerName},

  We wanted to let you know we experienced partial request failures and latency increases in US-west-2 between {start} and {end} UTC which may have affected calls routed to inference-service-us-west-2. Our SRE team identified a rollout-induced regression and performed a targeted rollback at {rollback_time}, which restored normal traffic patterns. We are investigating root cause and will provide a detailed postmortem by {pm_due_date}. If you need credits or other remediation, please reply and include any request IDs.

  Regards,
  Redwood Inference Support

Escalation & Regulatory Notes
- If the incident affects an enterprise tenant under contract that requires regulatory evidence, flag Legal and Compliance within 30 minutes and capture full evidence set.
- Preserve raw logs and do not delete artifacts until Compliance signs off.

Runbook Maintenance & Ownership
- Every runbook must have an owner and a last-verified date. Runbook verification cadence: quarterly for critical services; biannual for non-critical.
- Post-game-day requirement: the service owner must implement at least one improvement called out by the scorer within 30 days or provide a rebuttal.

Appendices
- Appendix A: Sample CLI snippets (already included above).
- Appendix B: Bridge poster template (copy into bridge invite): Incident ID, Ticket, Bridge lead, Primary, Secondary, Initial impact, Update cadence
- Appendix C: Quick-check dashboard links (Grafana dashboards, Kibana, SLO console) — list kept in the team runbook index.
